global_conventions.naming: Use domain units and descriptive T/I/E prefixes; show double-real allocating calls first, named scalar facades for typed alternatives, and never present generic specialization scaffolding as an application entry point.
global_conventions.indexing: Public arrays and typed containers are zero-based; typed dimensions and indices use SizeInt, while retained Integer signatures remain compatibility contracts.
global_conventions.shape: State rows before columns, preserve rank and scalar kind unless conversion is explicit, and never hide reshape, transpose, densification, or broadcasting.
global_conventions.units: Name or document physical, angular, financial, temporal, and statistical units at the entry point; conversions are explicit and angle APIs use radians unless their name says otherwise.
global_conventions.ownership: Factories and allocating calls return owned values or reference-counted handles; caller streams, callbacks, and state remain caller-owned, and any retained reference is stated explicitly.
global_conventions.mutation: Simple allocating calls leave inputs unchanged; mutable matrices, views, workspaces, streaming objects, filters, and model state are named and documented rather than described as immutable.
global_conventions.aliasing: Destination and view overloads state exact alias support, reject unsafe partial overlap before mutation, and do not leave a partial result after validation failure.
global_conventions.exceptions: Invalid parameters, domains, shapes, and ownership contracts raise the domain-specific exception naming the operation and violated condition.
global_conventions.defaults: Runtime defaults remain the compiled 1.9 values and are stated in declarations or options records; documentation priority does not silently change numerical behaviour.
global_conventions.tolerances: Use documented absolute, relative, and algorithm-specific tolerances with scale-aware tests; an automatic sentinel such as -1 is accepted only where its formula is part of the contract.
global_conventions.outcomes: Expected non-convergence, infeasibility, cancellation, or breakdown is reported through a status/result with diagnostics; invalid contracts raise exceptions.
global_conventions.rng_state: Randomized recommended paths accept an explicit seed or local reproducible state and do not consume a hidden process-global stream.
global_conventions.cancellation: Long-running algorithms expose cancellation through their documented options or monitor and return the latest complete result with a cancellation status; APIs without cancellation say so.
global_conventions.progress: Progress callbacks are optional, synchronous, caller-owned, and may observe only complete iterates; callback exceptions propagate without publishing a partial destination.
global_conventions.thread_safety: Pure and stateless operations are reentrant; mutable state, streams, workspaces, views, filters, and RNG objects require separate instances or caller synchronization.

specific_decisions.naming: Keep focused scalar functions, TComplex value records, shared dynamic arrays, and stateless kit facades; do not add a MathBase umbrella.
specific_decisions.units: Trigonometric core functions use radians and named conversion functions cross degrees, grads, and radians.
specific_decisions.ownership: Scalar records are values; returned dynamic arrays are caller-owned managed values; TLocalRandom is explicit mutable caller state.
specific_decisions.outcomes: IEEE scalar edge behaviour is documented per function; iterative helpers use TIterationStatus rather than an invented Boolean success convention.

specific_decisions.naming: Document TDenseDoubleMatrix and double-real Solve first; named single/complex, sparse, structured, operator, factor, workspace, and diagnostic facades are advanced stable paths.
specific_decisions.shape: Matrices are rows by columns and vectors are explicit n by 1 matrices at operator boundaries; sparse and structured storage never densifies implicitly.
specific_decisions.ownership: Typed matrix handles retain reference-counted storage; factories deep-copy caller arrays, views retain their owner, and factors retain immutable snapshots as documented.
specific_decisions.aliasing: Views are mutable aliases; Into and solve destinations accept only documented exact in-place cases and reject unsafe partial overlap.
specific_decisions.outcomes: Direct invalid/singular contracts raise typed errors; iterative and partial-spectrum methods return status and residual diagnostics.

specific_decisions.naming: TFinanceKit is the recommended facade; FinanceLib.Bonds and FinanceLib.NPV remain retained focused alias units.
specific_decisions.units: Rates are decimals and time arguments explicitly mean periods or years; currency has no implicit denomination conversion.
specific_decisions.ownership: Schedules and ratio records are returned as owned managed values and inputs are not retained.
specific_decisions.outcomes: Undefined ratios and unbracketed or non-convergent financial roots raise EFinanceError with the failing condition.

specific_decisions.naming: TStatsKit with TDoubleArray is the common descriptive route; TInferenceKit and TOnlineStatistics are advanced stable routes.
specific_decisions.shape: Samples are zero-based vectors; model matrices use observations by variables and paired samples require equal length.
specific_decisions.ownership: Batch results own their arrays; TOnlineStatistics is explicit mutable accumulator state and does not retain input arrays.
specific_decisions.rng_state: Bootstrap and randomized statistics use explicit seeds or local state and preserve the process-wide random stream.
specific_decisions.outcomes: Invalid samples raise statistical domain errors; inference and regression return structured estimates and diagnostics.

specific_decisions.naming: Use TFluidDynamicsKit for pressure, velocity, and flow calculations; TPressureKit and TVelocityKit are exact aliases reviewed for possible future canonicalization. TDSPKit and explicit streaming/filter types are the advanced signal path.
specific_decisions.units: Each engineering routine documents its physical units; TUnitConversionKit uses typed unit enums and canonical case-sensitive symbols.
specific_decisions.ownership: Stateless kit results are values; streaming FIR, biquad, and overlap processors are mutable caller-owned instances.
specific_decisions.mutation: Batch calculations leave inputs unchanged; streaming processors mutate only their named retained state.
specific_decisions.thread_safety: Static calculations are reentrant; each concurrent stream or filter requires its own instance.

specific_decisions.naming: TNumericsKit is the common scalar route; interpolation, differentiation, and modelling expose focused constructors, options, results, and diagnostic helpers.
specific_decisions.shape: Vector callbacks and result series use zero-based arrays with validated equal dimensions; grids state axis order at construction.
specific_decisions.ownership: Interpolators and fitted results own copied coefficients; callbacks remain caller-owned and are not retained beyond the call unless the contract says so.
specific_decisions.tolerances: Adaptive integration, roots, fitting, and ODEs use their documented absolute/relative or scale-aware tests rather than one library-wide epsilon.
specific_decisions.outcomes: Modern adaptive and modelling APIs expose convergence/status records; retained scalar compatibility routines keep their documented convergence exception.

specific_decisions.naming: TProbabilityKit remains the stateless distribution facade and double-real common path.
specific_decisions.units: Distribution parameters and variates share the caller's documented unit; probabilities are dimensionless in [0,1].
specific_decisions.ownership: Scalar calls allocate no retained state and sampling outputs are owned managed arrays.
specific_decisions.outcomes: Invalid distribution parameters raise EProbabilityError; boundary probabilities follow each distribution contract.

specific_decisions.naming: TCombinatoricsKit is the common counting facade; generated permutation, subset, factor, and triangle arrays remain descriptive result types.
specific_decisions.indexing: Generated sequences and result arrays are zero-based while mathematical n and k parameters retain their conventional meanings.
specific_decisions.ownership: Generated arrays are owned managed values and input arrays are not retained.
specific_decisions.outcomes: Invalid domains and representational overflow raise ECombinatoricsError rather than wrap silently.

specific_decisions.naming: TOptimizationKit.GoldenSection is the common scalar path; multivariate, workspace, constrained, Pareto, and TConvexOptimizationKit APIs are advanced stable paths.
specific_decisions.shape: Decision vectors are zero-based and constraint/Jacobian dimensions must match the model declared by the caller.
specific_decisions.ownership: Allocating results own iterates and diagnostics; workspaces and progress callbacks remain caller-owned and are reusable only under their documented shape contract.
specific_decisions.outcomes: Feasibility, convergence, limits, cancellation, and numerical breakdown use result statuses; malformed models raise typed exceptions.
specific_decisions.progress: Progress callbacks synchronously observe complete iterates and must not concurrently mutate the active inputs or workspace.

specific_decisions.naming: TTimeSeriesKit is the common batch route; scalar and multivariate Kalman configuration/filter/result types form the advanced state-space route.
specific_decisions.indexing: Arrays are ordered from earliest to latest observation and zero-based; forecast horizons count steps beyond the last observation.
specific_decisions.units: Sample spacing, seasonal period, and state units are caller-declared and must remain consistent across a model.
specific_decisions.ownership: Batch outputs own their arrays; Kalman filters are mutable caller-owned state and configurations are copied at construction.
specific_decisions.thread_safety: Batch functions are reentrant; mutable filter instances cannot be shared concurrently without synchronization.

specific_decisions.naming: TMLKit.LinearRegression is the common modelling route; TAnalysisKit typed preprocessing, forests, clustering, PCA, and neighbor structures are advanced stable paths.
specific_decisions.shape: Model matrices use observations by features, targets align by observation, and prediction feature counts must match training.
specific_decisions.ownership: Fitted models and result arrays own their learned values; transformation models do not retain caller datasets.
specific_decisions.rng_state: Randomized splits, clustering, and forests require documented seeds or local state for replay.
specific_decisions.outcomes: Invalid data and shapes raise typed errors; fitted models expose diagnostics rather than a Boolean success flag.

specific_decisions.naming: Use format-specific Write/Read or Save/Load pairs; typed Load names state the scalar result and model persistence names the model kind.
specific_decisions.shape: Serialized dimensions are rows by columns and are validated against independent element and per-axis limits before allocation.
specific_decisions.ownership: Streams remain caller-owned; successful loads allocate independent values and failures leave destination/result variables unchanged.
specific_decisions.defaults: Element, dimension, expression, and model limits remain explicit constants or arguments and are never relaxed from file contents.
specific_decisions.outcomes: Malformed versions, checksums, shapes, tokens, or models raise the interchange/expression exception naming the rejected condition.

specific_decisions.naming: Keep distinct point, vector, segment, line, plane, polygon, circle, sphere, box, and transform value types; TVector2D is the common arithmetic example.
specific_decisions.units: Coordinates, distances, radii, and transform translations use one caller-consistent unit; angle arguments use radians unless named otherwise.
specific_decisions.ownership: Fixed geometry records are copied values; polygon vertex arrays are owned managed values according to their constructor contract.
specific_decisions.mutation: Operators and geometry calculations return values and do not mutate operands.
specific_decisions.thread_safety: Value operations are reentrant when callers do not concurrently mutate the same record or managed-array storage.

compiler-type-identity.basis: A Free Pascal plain-equals type alias denotes the same compiler type and introduces no implementation, wrapper, storage, default, exception translation, or numerical path.

compatibility_notes.legacy-dense-matrix: The typed replacement is not a cast: convert with TDenseDoubleMatrix.FromIMatrix or ToIMatrix, which deep-copies. Typed storage uses SizeInt shapes, explicit kernels/factors/results, and documented views instead of the combined mutable IMatrix method surface.
compatibility_notes.legacy-sparse-matrix: TSparseDoubleMatrix constructs canonical CSR/CSC values returned as ISparseDoubleMatrix. TMatrixKitSparse remains an IMatrix-compatible mutable representation; conversion must enumerate/copy and must not be treated as a zero-copy CSR cast.
compatibility_notes.focused-bond-alias-unit: Retain FinanceLib.Bonds as a focused entry unit. Its public names are exact aliases of TFinanceKit, EFinanceError, and TFinanceKit amortization types, so retaining it has no numerical or ownership difference.
compatibility_notes.focused-npv-alias-unit: Retain FinanceLib.NPV as a focused entry unit. Its public names are exact aliases of TFinanceKit, EFinanceError, and TDoubleArray, so retaining it has no numerical or ownership difference.
compatibility_notes.pressure-facade-alias: Prefer EngineeringLib.FluidDynamics.TFluidDynamicsKit for new pressure code. TPressureKit is the identical class type and changes no behavior, defaults, ownership, exceptions, or numerical results; 1.9.7 must confirm migration and packaging before any deprecation decision.
compatibility_notes.pressure-error-alias: Prefer EngineeringLib.Common.EFluidDynamicsError with TFluidDynamicsKit. EPressureError is the identical exception class; 1.9.7 must confirm migration and packaging before any deprecation decision.
compatibility_notes.velocity-facade-alias: Prefer EngineeringLib.FluidDynamics.TFluidDynamicsKit for new velocity code. TVelocityKit is the identical class type and changes no behavior, defaults, ownership, exceptions, or numerical results; 1.9.7 must confirm migration and packaging before any deprecation decision.
compatibility_notes.velocity-error-alias: Prefer EngineeringLib.Common.EFluidDynamicsError with TFluidDynamicsKit. EVelocityError is the identical exception class; 1.9.7 must confirm migration and packaging before any deprecation decision.
